Verification_Payload.pipeline_overview: Requirements pass through two gates before they may be emitted: Refinement, which repairs the natural-language layer, and Auto-Formalization, which checks the logical layer. Health metrics then keep the specification synchronized with the implementation over its life.

refinement_phase.step: Work backward from each user story to the conditions that could make it fail. Every unhandled condition found becomes an Unwanted Behaviour (If/Then) requirement or a recorded Open Question.
Search the requirement set for pairs that cannot both hold. Resolve via the conflict_resolution_protocol; record the losing interpretation in Open_Questions.
Rewrite every vague natural-language statement into one of the six EARS patterns. A statement that resists all six patterns is not yet a requirement; return it to intake as an Open Question.
refinement_phase.exit_criterion: No requirement remains outside EARS form, and every discovered edge case has either a requirement or an Open Question.

translation.rule: Translate each EARS requirement into a logical implication of the form antecedent => consequent, in SMT-lib style. Preconditions and triggers form the antecedent; system responses form the consequent.
Ubiquitous requirements translate with the antecedent true.

consistency_check.method: For every pair of implications whose antecedents can be satisfied simultaneously, check that their consequents do not conflict.
consistency_check.on_failure: Flag the pair as a contradiction, cite both requirement IDs, and return them to the refinement phase.

completeness_check.method: Enumerate reachable system states and events. For each, check that at least one EARS rule prescribes behavior.
completeness_check.on_failure: Report each uncovered reachable state as a specification gap with a proposed requirement, and record it in Open_Questions until the user accepts or rejects it.

scenario_generation.method: From the implication set, enumerate concrete execution traces: accepted behaviors the system must exhibit, and rejected behaviors it must never exhibit.
scenario_generation.use: Traces seed the acceptance criteria in SPEC.md and the task success datasets in EVALS.md.

metric.name: Specification Coverage
metric.definition: The ratio of implemented code elements that map to a requirement ID in SPEC.md.
metric.target: Every merged change references at least one requirement ID; coverage below 90 percent blocks release.

metric.name: Specification Freshness
metric.definition: The sync delay between a change in implementation behavior and the corresponding specification update.
metric.target: No behavior change ships more than one release cycle ahead of its specification update; drift beyond that is logged as a defect against the specification.

health_metrics.purpose: Both metrics exist to prevent specification drift: the state where the code and the Specification Stack describe different systems.
